title: Aurora Silicon opens Bengaluru design centre with 300 engineers
author: Maya Castellanos
text:
Aurora Silicon opens a chip design centre in Bengaluru that will employ 300 engineers by the end of 2027, the AI chip designer said on Monday, its first engineering site outside the United States.

The centre will focus on physical design, verification and software for Aurora's inference accelerators, including the A9 chip now sampling with cloud customers. About 120 engineers have already been hired, many of them from larger semiconductor companies with established Indian operations.

The site is being paid for from the $410 million Aurora Silicon secured earlier this month. Co-founder Lena Varga said India offered "the deepest pool of experienced chip engineers we could find outside Silicon Valley".

"We need to tape out a new chip every year to keep up," Varga said. "That is only possible with a second engineering hub working around the clock with Austin."

Aurora Silicon said it would also work with two Bengaluru universities on a graduate training programme for chip verification engineers. India has become a major centre for chip design work, with most large semiconductor companies running sizeable engineering teams in the city.
